findings.element: states.phone and states.desk in render-b.js (lines 840 and 846)
findings.problem: Both guest states compose the identical parts as ownerSurface: horizon() + measure() + behindBlock() + foot(), with bar() and the editor host deleted. The guest is handed the couple's dashboard with the controls taken away. Nothing on it marks an arrival. Driven at 390, the first screenful reads: the couple's name, 79, DAYS, the date, the venue line, a rule, TODAY IS 16 JULY, and then the first substantive sentence a wedding guest ever reads from this company is a negative one, 'Nothing is planned until 1 August.', followed by roughly 200px of empty rule. The surface that decides opens on an absence. The owner surface earns its keep; the guest surface merely functions, and it is the one a stranger will judge the whole company by.
findings.fix: Add a guest-only opening block, rendered in states.phone and states.desk between horizon() and measure(), that carries the one positive fact the reader came for: the next moment and its distance, set as 'Menu tasting at The Orchard' at the sub-display step in 600 with 'in 16 days' beneath it in mono, both read through the existing accessor so the count cannot disagree with the measure. Demote the gap sentence from directly under the hero to inside the measure, printed at the gap it actually describes, at the body step in the quieter ink. Keep the count, the date and the venue line exactly as they are. The owner surface does not change.

findings.element: the .b-bubble string in states.unfurl (render-b.js line 983) and foot() (line 267)
findings.problem: The most human sentence anywhere in this review is 'Here is everything, love. It updates itself.' It is drawn in the mocked messaging bubble around the unfurl card, which is chrome the product does not own. Inside the artifact itself the sender exists only as 'Kept by Orla' in the mono micro step in the footer, below the fold on every guest surface. A person handing over the plan for the most important day of their life is given no place on the page to say a single word to the people receiving it, and the product borrows a warm line from an app it does not control to prove it has warmth.
findings.fix: Add an optional owner-authored note to the fixture (F.project.note, one sentence, cap 90 characters, unset on the empty project). Render it in states.phone, states.desk and states.print as a .b-handoff-note directly beneath the hero rule, at the body step in 400, with the attribution 'Orla' in the mono micro step on the following line. Render nothing at all when the field is unset, so a surface with no note is byte-identical to today. Add the same field to states.publish as a single-line input sitting above the link field, labelled 'Say something to them', so writing it is part of the act of handing over rather than a setting.

findings.element: the eight ahead dates in fixture.js (lines 81 to 87) and the 'Days away' label in measure() (render-b.js line 120)
findings.problem: Driven and measured, the measure is exactly linear at every scale: 14.0px per day at desk, 12.0 at phone, 10.0 in print, 18.0 for the owner, with no drift. That honesty is the one genuinely original idea in the product. But every interval in the fixture is 7 or 14 days, so the measure renders as even, even, double, even, even, double, double. It reads as a rhythm, not as a measurement, and nothing on any surface tells the reader that the space is the time. A discerning stranger sees uneven whitespace and files it as a layout inconsistency. The product's best idea is undemonstrated by the very frames chosen to demonstrate it.
findings.fix: Two changes. First, in fixture.js redistribute the eight ahead dates so density visibly varies against the same 3 October anchor: leave one stretch of at least 25 empty days in the middle, and put three moments inside the final ten days before the wedding, so the crush before the day is visible as shape rather than as a list. Second, in measure() add one line of body copy directly under the existing 'Days away' micro-label, rendered on guest surfaces and in print only: 'The space between them is the time between them.'

findings.element: row() in render-b.js (line 91), applied to the final ahead item on every guest and owner surface
findings.problem: The last row of the measure is '79 / Wedding day / SAT 3 OCT', drawn at exactly the size, weight and mark of 'Final dress fitting' and 'Choose the evening music'. The destination that every other number on the page is measured from arrives as the last bullet, gets a hairline over it, and is followed by a footer. The plan builds for 1276 pixels and then stops rather than lands. A countdown whose terminus carries no more emphasis than an errand is a countdown to nothing in particular.
findings.fix: In row(), set data-terminal="true" on the item whose date equals F.project.primaryDate.date. In b.css, draw that row one step up the existing type ramp at weight 600, fill its mark solid instead of stroking it hollow, and end the measure rule at the centre of that mark rather than running it past. No new colour, no new weight, no new radius: fill and one existing ramp step, which is exactly how this surface already expresses hierarchy.

findings.element: b.css: zero @keyframes in the whole file, six transition declarations, five of them colour and one on top
findings.problem: Driven across all eleven states at 390, 768, 1280 and 1440, every element in every state reports animationName 'none'. The entire motion budget of the product is one row sliding on the measure when the owner presses a stepper. The guest states carry between 0 and 7 transitions, all of them hover colour on a surface with nothing hoverable: phone, desk, day, unfurl, ended and loading paint and stop. The count does not arrive, it is simply already there. On the wedding morning the word 'Today' does not land, it is just painted. That word is the single memorable moment in this product and it is delivered with less ceremony than a page refresh.
findings.fix: One entrance, once, on guest surfaces only, inside the existing prefers-reduced-motion guard the gate already checks. The count rises 8px and fades 0 to 1 over 320ms on --ease. The measure marks then fade in over 240ms, staggered 24ms apart, capped at the first eight so a long plan does not crawl. Nothing loops and nothing replays on scroll. On the day state, 'Today' alone takes the same 320ms rise and everything else paints flat.

biggestWin: There is one memorable moment and it is real: on the wedding morning the count does not run out to zero, it becomes the word 'Today', set at the count's own display step with 'This is the day the plan was for.' underneath it. That is a designed decision with feeling in it, and it is the reason this is a 7.3 and not a 6. Everything around it is beautifully set and emotionally inert. The typography is genuinely expensive: Geist at display scale for 79 and for Today is confident, the three-colour discipline holds without ever looking impoverished, and the copy is the best thing in the build. 'When is the day? Everything on this page is measured from it, so it is the only thing needed to start' is a better empty state than most funded companies ship. 'Nothing has been deleted. Only the link stopped working' is exactly the sentence a frightened person needs. The owner surface is fully built and fully reversible, driven end to end: every row opens on Enter, focus enters the editor and returns to the row that opened it on Escape, the reversibility bar announces the change it actually made ('Send the invitations moved 7 days later. Undo Ctrl Z'), Ctrl+Z restores a deleted moment, and delete never drops focus to the body. Zero console errors in forty-four state and width combinations. Would a discerning stranger believe a top studio made this? Looking at the owner surface, yes. Looking at what a guest gets, they would believe a very good designer set it, and they would feel nothing. They would not reach for a card. What stands between this and 9.5 is not polish. It is one decision plus one build. The decision is whether the guest artifact is the owner's page with the chrome removed or a different object entirely, because right now it is provably the former: states.phone and states.desk call the same four functions ownerSurface calls, minus the buttons. The build is small and specific: an arrival for the guest, a place for the sender to speak, a fixture that lets the measure show what it means, and one entrance motion. That is a direction round and a build round. Days, not weeks.
